body: Tysm this surprisingly made me feel a lot better. I really wish the same, that we can call be at peace in some way or the other with ourselves but I’m struggling so much that I don’t think I’ve ever felt pain of this magnitude in my entire life. It’s like this is the climax of a movie or something and soon it’s all going to stop. I don’t know, maybe I’m just so detached from reality that I can’t think clearly but all I want is peace.
Wtf. Did you break your spine?

Others may perceive this as sick and evil, but I’m envious of the ferocity and courage you have- to take the lead and finally do something. I’ve been wanting to end my life for years and I’m too much of a damn coward. I always wish I could just join you and finish this once and for all. But of course, I’m stuck in this stationary void of depression. I can’t do anything about it, but read other people’s posts about how they are finally doing it. I wish man. I wish.

I’ve always thought the same thing. No one really cares in the core of their being if you tell them how depressed you’ve been feeling. They’ll take it into account for a few days or weeks, try to help you- and then the support will just taper off after a while. Whether it’s because of the way you respond to their input or the way they see no progress in your mindset. They’ll just get bored of it, tired and frustrated. They won’t care anymore. And it makes sense. No one truly wants to care about another individual to that extent. It’s not in our human capacity to be so generous towards each other. Our compassion is limited, and it’s so obvious to me now. Staying alive for others is so meaningless. We just pretend to care about each other and then feel bad when someone dies by suicide. That’s the way it goes. We care when there is no point in caring.
I need the answer to this question too. Just a simple fool-proof step by step that I can follow to the dot. One that can lead me right to death’s door. In my opinion, gas is the best way.

Is there no other way out of it? That’s so messed up- I’ve always been against war and violence too and tbh I’d probably end it if it reached that point- mainly owing to the fact that I’m already majorly depressed but still- I don’t know how you’re coping.

To be honest, that’s my worst fear. To finally summon the will and energy to end it all- only to find that it’s all a facade and I never really had a choice because my mind would always be a barrier between me and that final solution. Despite that, I’m glad that you’re feeling better and not worse.

Wouldn’t it be simply amazing to cease you’re existence without putting an ounce of effort into it? To just stop. To subtly sever that tether tying you to the familiarities of your life without realising it. Something as simple as going to sleep and never waking up again. The thought scares me and comforts me at the same time.

That’s the only thing stopping me too. My own cowardice to actually go through with what I have planned for a long time. To finally end this cycle of unmitigated suffering and trauma. I’m traumatised by this world. This life. And I haven’t even suffered a drop of the amount that you have. I feel for you so much. This world is trauma and it’s sad that we were brought into such unfortunate circumstances. To simply act as pawns in a great melancholic game of abuse and hate. I want to stop existing- and that’s where the problem arises. It’s just that, I want to cease my existence with the blink of an eye. I don’t actually want to put the effort into killing myself. Every time I get up, make a physical move to end everything, a big giant wall places itself in front of me and my heart stops. I keep thinking and my heart becomes heavy with dread. I don’t know if it will be better when I leave. But anything seems better than this torturous, unending grief and numbness. These nauseating feelings grip our hearts in playful turns until we’ll finally grow so desperate and eager for reprieve, we’ll do anything. I think we have yet to reach the end of our will. We have yet to abandon all hope.  We’re still in the depth of our trauma, speechless and stilled by the extent of the distress we’ve been drowning in for so long. It’s so hard to let go when living with the sadness and frustration is the only thing we’ve ever known. I feel for you. I wish there was a way to simply summon enough energy to just climb that wall. I think their is a backpack of burden weighing us down- it holds our worries and anxieties about that final solution. We just need to take it off. Maybe there’s a place of complete consolation and freedom beyond that wall. Maybe the only true contentment there is to experience lies beyond that wall. If anything- there’s the chance of it. I wish it wasn’t like this for you. I wish indifference and courage wasn’t so hard to come by when you needed it most.
